title: Paloma and the Verdict
premise: When the coffin of Halvard Maren, founder of the tidal town of Greywater, is exhumed for a memorial reburial and found empty, concierge Vesper Nystrom recognizes a guest from ten years ago in the funeral photographs — a man who checked in the week Halvard supposedly died and never checked out. As the sheriff's office fumbles a case file that seems to have been rewritten from within, Vesper uses her hotel's ledgers, keys, and long memory to reconstruct what really happened: Halvard faked his death to escape prosecution, and the man who helped him has been killing everyone who could prove it. Vesper lures the killer into confessing at the tide-flattened cove where the body was hidden, and the sea finally gives up its secret — but only after she must choose between exposing a friend who protected the lie and telling the truth that will break the town.
about_author: Oscar Nystrom is a former night-shift hotelier who spent a decade logging the comings and goings of strangers in a coastal town not unlike Greywater. He writes mysteries about the quiet observers — the people behind desks who see everything and are believed by no one.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Vesper Nystrom, concierge at the Hotel Meridian, watches the town of Greywater exhume its founder Halvard Maren for a centennial reburial — and sees the pallbearers' faces when the coffin proves empty. POV Vesper. Beat: dread beneath ceremony; her instinct that something is wrong before anyone says it aloud.

chapters.title: Guest Register
chapters.summary: Sheriff's deputy Ilsa Brand interviews hotel staff; Vesper quietly pulls the old ledgers and finds an anomaly — a guest, Mr. Renn, checked in the week of Halvard's death ten years ago with no checkout date. POV Vesper. Beat: the thrill of the hunt awakening; she notices everything, and now noticing is dangerous.

chapters.title: A Case File Rewritten
chapters.summary: Deputy Brand discovers the original death-investigation file has pages replaced with flawless forgeries — someone inside law enforcement tampered. POV Brand. Beat: institutional vertigo; the law itself becomes untrustworthy, planting the justice-outside-the-law theme.

chapters.title: The Founder's Daughter
chapters.summary: Maren's heir, Odile Maren, hires Vesper informally to discreetly investigate before the scandal ruins the family name and the hotel with it. POV Vesper. Beat: reluctant complicity; loyalty offered as a leash, and Vesper accepting it for reasons she doesn't fully admit.

chapters.title: Room 214
chapters.summary: Vesper searches the long-sealed Room 214 where Mr. Renn stayed and finds a hidden tide chart annotated with dates after Halvard's supposed death. POV Vesper. Beat: cold clarity — Halvard may have staged his own death, and someone has been keeping the secret for a decade.

chapters.title: What the Tide Takes
chapters.summary: A crab fisherman dredges up a rotted suitcase containing Halvard's real remains — killed, not vanished. POV Brand. Beat: the case turns from scandal to murder; the town's grief curdles into suspicion of everyone.

chapters.title: The Man Who Never Left
chapters.summary: Vesper traces Mr. Renn's identity to Corvin Ashe, the former deputy who handled the original file — and who now serves as the town's beloved archivist. POV Vesper. Beat: the horror of recognizing evil wearing a trusted face; loyalty to the town vs. the truth.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Small Kindnesses
chapters.summary: Vesper reviews a decade of Ashe's quiet favors — funeral flowers, sealed records, redirected mail — and maps a pattern of cover-up maintenance. POV Vesper. Beat: chilling admiration; power corrupting through patience rather than violence, so far.

chapters.title: Odile's Alibi
chapters.summary: Brand suspects Odile Maren of hiring the exhumation to bury her father's crimes; Vesper defends her but notices Odile lied about one detail — she knew the coffin was empty before it was opened. POV Brand. Beat: shifting alliances; even the client is compromised.

chapters.title: The Second Death
chapters.summary: The retired coroner who signed the original death certificate drowns in his bathtub hours after Vesper interviews him. POV Brand. Beat: escalation and guilt; Vesper realizes her questions painted a target on him.

chapters.title: Keys and Ledgers
chapters.summary: Ashe visits the hotel, charming and watchful, and returns a key Vesper 'lost' — a message that he knows she's searching. POV Vesper. Beat: cat-and-mouse begins in earnest; fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Confession That Wasn't
chapters.summary: A drifter confesses to Halvard's murder, and the town wants to believe him; Vesper proves his timeline impossible using tide tables and the hotel's laundry logs. POV Vesper. Beat: frustration with a town eager for easy justice; her outsider status as both shield and cage.

chapters.title: What Odile Bought
chapters.summary: Vesper confronts Odile, who admits Halvard staged his death to flee embezzlement charges, and Ashe — then a young deputy — helped him for a share, then killed him when he tried to come back. POV Odile. Beat: the family's rot exposed; loyalty as the currency of corruption.

chapters.title: Brand's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Brand finds evidence implicating her own mentor, the retired sheriff, in the file tampering, and must decide whether to report it and destroy her career's foundation. POV Brand. Beat: the theme made personal — the law protecting itself instead of the truth.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: Someone ransacks the hotel archives; Vesper, hiding, watches Ashe photograph the ledgers and burn what he can't carry. POV Vesper. Beat: terror and confirmation; the hunt inverts and she becomes the hunted.

chapters.title: The Trap Takes Shape
chapters.summary: Vesper and Brand, unable to arrest Ashe on evidence that won't survive his insider knowledge, plan to make him confess at the cove where he hid the suitcase, using a forged letter claiming Halvard's accomplice kept a written insurance policy. POV both. Beat: desperate ingenuity; justice built outside the law because the law is compromised.

chapters.title: Low Tide
chapters.summary: The sting begins at the cove at low tide; Ashe arrives, sees through part of the ruse, and turns it back on them, revealing he's already framed Vesper for the coroner's death. POV Vesper. Beat: the trap springs the wrong way; despair at the killer's mastery of the case file.

chapters.title: What the Sea Kept
chapters.summary: Ashe takes Vesper to the sea cave where Halvard died to finish the job; she stalls him with the one detail he can't explain — why Halvard's watch was found stopped at a time the tides don't match his story. POV Vesper. Beat: wit as weapon; her lifetime of noticing becomes the blade.

chapters.title: The Turning Water
chapters.summary: Brand, having chosen truth over loyalty to her mentor, arrives with the recovered original file pages Ashe never found — hidden by the dead coroner. Ashe, cornered by the rising tide and the record, confesses. POV Brand. Beat: climax; the law redeemed only by an act of personal courage.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Ashe is arrested; in the aftermath, the town learns Halvard was a thief and a victim both, and Odile must decide what to do with the inheritance. POV Vesper. Beat: bittersweet justice; the truth costs more than anyone budgeted.

chapters.title: The Friend Who Knew
chapters.summary: Vesper discovers her oldest friend at the hotel, Marta, knew about the cover-up for years and kept silent to protect the town's fragile economy — and must choose whether to report her. POV Vesper. Beat: the loyalty-vs-truth theme lands on the one relationship Vesper can't afford to lose.

chapters.title: High Water Mark
chapters.summary: Months later, Halvard is reburied — in a coffin that holds him this time — and Vesper, promoted to general manager, watches the tide come in clean. Marta has left town; Vesper keeps her secret and her sorrow. POV Vesper. Beat: resolution; the sea gives back what it took, and Vesper learns some verdicts are carried, not delivered.
